source.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְשָׁלֹשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן־אֲחַזְיָ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָחָ֨ז בֶּן־יֵה֤וּא עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן שְׁבַ֥ע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In year twenty and three year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah reigned Jehoahaz son of Jehu over Israel in Samaria seven-teen year[s].

en.L: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria seventeen years.
en.B: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.
en.R: Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in the twenty-third year that Joash son of Ahaziah was king of Judah. He ruled from Samaria for seventeen years.

decisions.choice: reigned ... seventeen years: became king and reigned seventeen years
decisions.reason: One verb does both jobs, as in the accession formula elsewhere in Kings (1 Kings 15:33): it dates the start of the reign and, with the number, gives its length.

decisions.choice: Jehoahaz son of Jehu: the second king of Jehu's dynasty
decisions.reason: Jehu had wiped out the house of Ahab and taken the throne (9:1-10:28); Jehoahaz followed him when he died (10:35). Yahweh had promised Jehu that his sons would sit on Israel's throne to the fourth generation (10:30).

decisions.choice: Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah: the boy king saved from Athaliah
decisions.reason: This Joash was hidden as a baby and made king of Judah at seven (11:1-12:1). At this time Israel's king Jehoahaz also has a son named Joash (verse 9), so two kings of the same name reign side by side for a time.

decisions.choice: and he reigned
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the verb twice, "became king" and "reigned", as the accession formula does at this level throughout Kings. Readable splits it into two sentences.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַ֠יֵּלֶךְ אַחַ֨ר חַטֹּ֜את יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּן־נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר־הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹא־סָ֥ר מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh and walked after [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he made sin Israel; not he turned aside from it.

en.L: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he walked after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel sin; he did not turn aside from it.
en.B: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he led Israel to sin; he did not turn away from them.
en.R: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He kept on in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, the sins by which Jeroboam led Israel into sin. He did not turn away from them.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat: the worship at the golden calves of Bethel and Dan
decisions.reason: Jeroboam set up the calves so that Israel would not go to Jerusalem to worship (1 Kings 12:26-33). Jehu destroyed Baal worship but kept these shrines (10:29, 31), and his son does the same. Kings judges every king of Israel by this sin.

decisions.choice: made Israel sin: caused the nation to sin
decisions.reason: The verb is causative: Jeroboam led the whole people into sin, and each later king who kept his shrines shared in it (1 Kings 16:2).

decisions.choice: from it: from that sin as a whole
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular though "sins" is plural. It gathers Jeroboam's sins together as one way of worship.

decisions.choice: the verdict and the sin of Jeroboam in their fixed wording
decisions.reason: The verdict formula keeps one wording at each level through Kings: "did the evil in [the] eyes of" (Literal), "did what was evil in the sight of" (Balanced), "did what the LORD said was evil" (Readable). The formula of the sin of Jeroboam keeps one wording at each level through Kings, as at 3:3: "made Israel sin" (Literal), "led Israel to sin" (Balanced), "led Israel into sin" (Readable).

decisions.choice: followed / kept on in; from them
decisions.reason: "Walked after" means followed as a way of life. Balanced and Readable say "them" for the singular "it", since English speaks of the sins in the plural (m3).

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֞ם בְּיַ֣ד׀חֲזָאֵ֣ל מֶֽלֶךְ־אֲרָ֗ם וּבְיַ֛ד בֶּן־הֲדַ֥ד בֶּן־חֲזָאֵ֖ל כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against Israel, and he gave them into [the] hand of Hazael king of Aram and into [the] hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael all the days.

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them into [the] hand of Hazael king of Aram and into [the] hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael all the days.
en.B: So the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them into the power of Hazael king of Aram and of Ben-hadad son of Hazael throughout that time.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became angry with Israel. He handed them over to Hazael king of Aram and to his son Ben-hadad for all those years.

decisions.choice: the anger of Yahweh burned: Yahweh became angry
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as a fire that flares up, as in Judges 2:14, 20. The cause is the sin of verse 2.

decisions.choice: gave them into the hand of: put them under the power of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and control, the language of Judges (Judges 2:14; 6:1). Yahweh lets Aram overpower Israel.

decisions.choice: Hazael and his son Ben-hadad: kings of Aram, ruling from Damascus
decisions.reason: Elisha had wept when he foresaw the harm Hazael would do to Israel (8:11-13), and Hazael had already taken all Israel's land east of the Jordan in Jehu's day (10:32-33). His son bore a name used by earlier kings of Aram (1 Kings 15:18; 20:1).

decisions.choice: all the days: continually, through that period
decisions.reason: The phrase means the pressure did not let up. Verse 22 says Hazael oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz, and the cities were not won back until Ben-hadad's time (verse 25).

decisions.choice: gave them into the power of (Balanced); handed them over to (Readable); throughout that time / for all those years
decisions.reason: As in Judges, Balanced turns "hand" into "power" and Readable says "handed them over". Readable calls Ben-hadad "his son" where the Hebrew says "son of Hazael".

source.text: וַיְחַ֥ל יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֤י רָאָה֙ אֶת־לַ֣חַץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּֽי־לָחַ֥ץ אֹתָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ אֲרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And entreated Jehoahaz [the] face of Yahweh, and listened to him Yahweh, for he saw the oppression of Israel, that oppressed them [the] king of Aram.

en.L: And Jehoahaz entreated the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to him, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the oppression of Israel, that the king of Aram oppressed them.
en.B: Then Jehoahaz pleaded with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for favor, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to him, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw how the king of Aram was oppressing Israel.
en.R: Then Jehoahaz begged {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to him. He saw how harshly the king of Aram was treating Israel.

decisions.choice: entreated the face of Yahweh: pleaded with Yahweh for his favor
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures softening someone's face, that is, seeking to turn his anger into kindness. Moses prays in the same words in Exodus 32:11, and a king of Israel asks a prophet to do so in 1 Kings 13:6.

decisions.choice: he saw the oppression of Israel: the pattern of the exodus and of Judges
decisions.reason: The words echo Yahweh seeing the oppression of Israel in Egypt (Exodus 3:9) and having pity on them because of those who oppressed them in the days of the judges (Judges 2:18). A king who does evil still finds that Yahweh answers his people's distress.

decisions.choice: pleaded with ... for favor / begged ... for help; oppressing / treating harshly
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sense of the idiom, "for favor"; Readable says what Jehoahaz asked for. Readable uses "treating harshly" for "oppress", here and in verse 22.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֤ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מוֹשִׁ֔יעַ וַיֵּ֣צְא֔וּ מִתַּ֖חַת יַד־אֲרָ֑ם וַיֵּשְׁב֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּאָהֳלֵיהֶ֖ם כִּתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Yahweh to Israel a deliverer, and they went out from under [the] hand of Aram, and dwelt [the] sons of Israel in their tents as yesterday [and] three days ago.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel a deliverer, and they went out from under the hand of Aram, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel dwelt in their tents as yesterday [and] the day before.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped from the power of Aram. So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lived in their homes as they had before.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel someone to rescue them, and they were set free from Aram's control. Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lived in their own homes again, as they had in earlier times.

decisions.choice: a deliverer: one who rescues from enemies
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the judges whom Yahweh raised up to rescue Israel (Judges 3:9, 15). Yahweh's answer to Jehoahaz follows the pattern of that book (verse 4).

decisions.choice: the deliverer is not named
alternatives: relief through Assyria's attacks on Aram
decisions.reason: The writer does not say who he was. He may be Jehoash, who won back Israel's cities (verse 25), or Jeroboam son of Jehoash, through whom Yahweh saved Israel (14:25-27). It is also possible that the relief came from outside: in these years the kings of Assyria pressed hard on Damascus, which drew Aram's strength away from Israel.

decisions.choice: dwelt in their tents: lived at home in peace
decisions.reason: "Tents" had come to mean homes in general, long after Israel lived in tents (1 Kings 8:66; 12:16). The people no longer had to flee or hide from raiders.

decisions.choice: as yesterday and the day before: as in former times
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as before" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:7).

decisions.choice: deliverer / someone to rescue them; homes
decisions.reason: Readable follows Judges 3:9 in saying what a deliverer is. Balanced and Readable say "homes" for "tents" (m3); Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: אַ֠ךְ לֹֽא־סָ֜רוּ מֵחַטֹּ֧אות בֵּית־יָרָבְעָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣הּ הָלָ֑ךְ וְגַם֙ הָאֲשֵׁרָ֔ה עָמְדָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Only not they turned aside from [the] sins of [the] house of Jeroboam which he made sin Israel; in it he walked; and also the Asherah stood in Samaria.

en.L: Yet they did not turn aside from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, which he made Israel sin; in it he walked. And also the Asherah pole stood in Samaria.
en.B: Yet they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, by which he led Israel to sin, but kept walking in them. The Asherah pole also remained standing in Samaria.
en.R: But the people did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam's dynasty, the sins by which Jeroboam led Israel into sin. They kept on living in those sins. And the pole used to worship Asherah still stood in Samaria.

decisions.choice: the house of Jeroboam: Jeroboam and the kings who kept his worship
decisions.reason: "House" here is a royal line. Jeroboam's own family was wiped out (1 Kings 15:29), but the sins he began were kept up by every king of Israel after him, so they are still called the sins of his house.

decisions.choice: in it he walked: Israel kept living in that sin
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, with Israel as one people as its likely subject; it could also be Jehoahaz. Either way the deliverance of verse 5 did not bring the nation back to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: the Asherah: the pole of the goddess Asherah that Ahab set up
decisions.reason: Ahab had made an Asherah pole in Samaria (1 Kings 16:33). Jehu destroyed the temple of Baal (10:26-28) but left this pole standing. The verb means it remained in place through these years.

decisions.choice: Asherah pole (Literal, Balanced); the pole used to worship Asherah (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for Asherah poles in Samuel and Kings (1 Kings 16:33).

decisions.choice: the sin formula; walking in them / living in those sins
decisions.reason: The formula of the sin of Jeroboam keeps one wording at each level through Kings, as at 3:3: "made Israel sin" (Literal), "led Israel to sin" (Balanced), "led Israel into sin" (Readable). Balanced and Readable say "them" for the singular "it", as in verse 2, and Readable names "the people" as the subject.

source.text: כִּ֣י לֹא֩ הִשְׁאִ֨יר לִיהוֹאָחָ֜ז עָ֗ם כִּ֣י אִם־חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים פָּֽרָשִׁים֙ וַעֲשָׂ֣רָה רֶ֔כֶב וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים רַגְלִ֑י כִּ֤י אִבְּדָם֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם וַיְשִׂמֵ֥ם כֶּֽעָפָ֖ר לָדֻֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: For not he left to Jehoahaz people except fifty horsemen and ten chariot[s] and ten thousand foot soldier[s], for destroyed them [the] king of Aram and made them like the dust for trampling.

en.L: For he did not leave to Jehoahaz [any] people except fifty horsemen and ten chariots and 10,000 foot soldiers, for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust for trampling.
en.B: Jehoahaz had been left with no troops except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and 10,000 foot soldiers, because the king of Aram had wiped them out and made them like dust to be trampled.
en.R: Jehoahaz had only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and 10,000 foot soldiers left in his army. The king of Aram had destroyed the rest. He had crushed them like dust that is trampled underfoot.

decisions.choice: for: verse 7 explains the distress of verse 4
decisions.reason: Verses 5-6 are an aside that looks ahead to the rescue and back to Israel's sin. Verse 7 returns to the time of Jehoahaz's prayer and shows how weak Israel had become.

decisions.choice: he did not leave: the king of Aram left Jehoahaz this little
decisions.reason: The subject is not named at first; the end of the verse shows it is the king of Aram. Behind him stands Yahweh, who gave Israel into his power (verse 3).

decisions.choice: people: an army
decisions.reason: The word for "people" often means the fighting men of a nation. Fifty horsemen and ten chariots are next to nothing beside the two thousand chariots Ahab sent against Assyria a generation before, and beside the chariots David and Solomon had (1 Kings 10:26).

decisions.choice: like the dust for trampling: crushed as grain is threshed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of threshing grain by treading it. Amos says Hazael threshed Gilead with iron sledges (Amos 1:3), and Elisha had foretold that Hazael would crush Israel's fighting men (8:12).

decisions.choice: [any] people (Literal); troops (Balanced); army (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the word "people" when it means an army in the field. Balanced and Readable use a passive, "had been left", so that the subject is not mistaken for Yahweh (m2).

decisions.choice: destroyed the rest
decisions.reason: Readable says "the rest": the king of Aram destroyed the army apart from the few who remained.

source.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֧י יְהוֹאָחָ֛ז וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה וּגְבוּרָת֑וֹ הֲלוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Jehoahaz and all that he did and his might, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Israel?

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
en.B: The rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, all that he did and his might, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.
en.R: Everything else about Jehoahaz, all he did and his great deeds, is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: a royal record now lost
decisions.reason: Kings names the records it drew on (1 Kings 14:19; 2 Kings 1:18). This one was a history of the kings of Israel; it has not survived, and the writer sends readers to it for what he leaves out.

decisions.choice: are they not written ...?: a question that means "they are written"
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes. It is the standard closing formula for a reign.

decisions.choice: his might: his strength and deeds in war
decisions.reason: The formula speaks of a king's might even where, as here, his army had been reduced to almost nothing (verse 7). It is the fixed wording for every reign.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel (Literal); the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel (Balanced); the history of the kings of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: The source formula has one wording at each level throughout Kings. Balanced and Readable turn the question into a statement (m2).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהֽוֹאָחָז֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And lay down Jehoahaz with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and reigned Joash his son in his place.

en.L: And Jehoahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and Joash his son reigned in his place.
en.B: Jehoahaz rested with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. His son Joash became king in his place.
en.R: Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria. His son Joash became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: This is the formula Kings uses for a king's death (1 Kings 2:10; 2 Kings 10:35).

decisions.choice: Joash: the same king as Jehoash in verse 10
decisions.reason: Joash is a short form of the name Jehoash, and the chapter uses both for this king of Israel (verses 10, 25). He is a different man from Joash king of Judah (verse 1), who reigned at the same time.

decisions.choice: the death formula; Joash
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings. The king's name follows the form each verse uses, Joash or Jehoash, at every level.

source.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹאָ֖שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יְהוֹאָ֨שׁ בֶּן־יְהוֹאָחָ֤ז עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In year thirty and seven year of Joash king of Judah reigned Jehoash son of Jehoahaz over Israel in Samaria six-teen year[s].

en.L: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz reigned over Israel in Samaria sixteen years.
en.B: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.
en.R: Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in the thirty-seventh year that Joash was king of Judah. He ruled from Samaria for sixteen years.

decisions.choice: the thirty-seventh year: the dates do not add up simply
alternatives: a shared reign of father and son
different ways of counting reign years in Judah and Israel
decisions.reason: Jehoahaz began in Joash's twenty-third year and reigned seventeen years (verse 1), which would bring his son's accession to about Joash's thirty-ninth year, not his thirty-seventh. The difference may come from a time when father and son reigned together, or from Judah and Israel counting a king's first part-year in different ways. The numbers are kept as the text gives them.

decisions.choice: Jehoash: the full form of the name Joash
decisions.reason: See verse 9.

decisions.choice: and he reigned
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מִכָּל־חַטֹּ֞אות יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּן־נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר־הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֥הּ הָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh; not he turned aside from all [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he made sin Israel; in it he walked.

en.L: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; he did not turn aside from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel sin; in it he walked.
en.B: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he led Israel to sin, but walked in them.
en.R: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, the sins by which Jeroboam led Israel into sin. He kept on living in them.

decisions.choice: the same verdict as for his father
decisions.reason: Jehoash kept Jeroboam's calf worship, as Jehoahaz did (verse 2). Even so, Yahweh gives him victories over Aram (verses 17-19, 25).

decisions.choice: in it he walked: Jehoash kept living in that sin
decisions.reason: Here the subject is the king himself. As in verse 2, the singular "it" gathers the sins as one.

decisions.choice: the verdict and the sin of Jeroboam in their fixed wording
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

source.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י יוֹאָשׁ֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וּגְב֣וּרָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִלְחַ֔ם עִ֖ם אֲמַצְיָ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Joash and all that he did and his might with which he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Israel?

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Joash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
en.B: The rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did and the might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.
en.R: Everything else Joash did, including his great deeds and his war against Amaziah king of Judah, is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: he fought with Amaziah king of Judah: the war told in 14:8-14
decisions.reason: Amaziah, the son of Joash of Judah, challenged Jehoash and was defeated at Beth-shemesh. The same closing formula is given again after that story (14:15-16).

decisions.choice: fought with: fought against
decisions.reason: With this verb, "with" names the enemy.

decisions.choice: the source formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹאָשׁ֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וְיָרָבְעָ֖ם יָשַׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְא֑וֹ וַיִּקָּבֵ֤ר יוֹאָשׁ֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן עִ֖ם מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And lay down Joash with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne; and was buried Joash in Samaria with [the] kings of Israel.

en.L: And Joash lay down with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. And Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
en.B: Joash rested with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
en.R: Joash died, and his son Jeroboam took his place as king. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the reign is closed before the stories of Elisha's death and the wars with Aram
decisions.reason: Kings ends its account of Jehoash here, then tells events from within his reign (verses 14-25). The order groups the stories around Elisha rather than following time strictly.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam: the son of Jehoash, the second king of Israel with this name
decisions.reason: This is not Jeroboam son of Nebat but Jeroboam son of Joash, who reigned forty-one years and won back much of Israel's land (14:23-28).

decisions.choice: sat on his throne: became king after him
decisions.reason: Kings usually says "reigned in his place" (verse 9); this wording means the same.

decisions.choice: his son Jeroboam; took his place as king
decisions.reason: Readable adds "his son" from 14:23, so that this Jeroboam is not confused with Jeroboam son of Nebat, and explains "sat on his throne".

source.text: וֶֽאֱלִישָׁע֙ חָלָ֣ה אֶת־חָלְי֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָמ֖וּת בּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֨רֶד אֵלָ֜יו יוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיֵּ֤בְךְּ עַל־פָּנָיו֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָבִ֣י׀אָבִ֔י רֶ֥כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּפָרָשָֽׁיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And Elisha was sick [with] his sickness which he would die by it; and went down to him Joash king of Israel and wept over his face and said, My father, my father! [The] chariotry of Israel and its horsemen!

en.L: And Elisha had fallen sick with his sickness of which he would die. And Joash king of Israel went down to him and wept over his face and said, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!"
en.B: Now Elisha had fallen ill with the sickness that would bring his death. Joash king of Israel went down to see him and wept over him. He said, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!"
en.R: Elisha became sick with the illness that would end his life. Joash king of Israel went down to see him. He wept over him and cried, "My father, my father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!"

decisions.choice: Elisha had fallen sick: a new story set in Joash's reign
decisions.reason: The verse turns back from the close of the reign (verse 13) to an event within it. Elisha has not been seen since he sent a prophet to anoint Jehu (9:1); he had served as a prophet since the days of Ahab's sons.

decisions.choice: wept over his face: bent over the dying man and wept
decisions.reason: The king comes to the sickbed and mourns the prophet before he dies.

decisions.choice: My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!: Elisha's own cry when Elijah was taken
decisions.reason: Elisha said these words as Elijah went up (2:12). The prophet through whom Yahweh worked was Israel's true defense, worth more than its chariots. On the king's lips the words are the more striking because Israel now has only ten chariots and fifty horsemen (verse 7). "My father" is a title of honor; Joash of Israel used it for Elisha before (6:21).

decisions.choice: the cry worded as in 2:12
decisions.reason: The cry repeats 2:12 word for word at each level, so the reader hears the echo. The Hebrew "chariot" is singular but means chariots as a force.

decisions.choice: wept over him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "over him" for "over his face" (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אֱלִישָׁ֔ע קַ֖ח קֶ֣שֶׁת וְחִצִּ֑ים וַיִּקַּ֥ח אֵלָ֖יו קֶ֥שֶׁת וְחִצִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Elisha, Take a bow and arrows; and he took to himself a bow and arrows.

en.L: And Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." And he took to himself a bow and arrows.
en.B: Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took a bow and arrows.
en.R: Elisha told him, "Get a bow and some arrows." So the king got a bow and arrows.

decisions.choice: take a bow and arrows: the start of an acted sign
decisions.reason: Prophets often acted out a message so that the action itself carried Yahweh's word (1 Kings 11:29-31; 22:11). What the king does with the bow and arrows in verses 16-19 shows what will happen in his war with Aram.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names the king where the Hebrew says only "he".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לְמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַרְכֵּ֤ב יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל־הַקֶּ֔שֶׁת וַיַּרְכֵּ֖ב יָד֑וֹ וַיָּ֧שֶׂם אֱלִישָׁ֛ע יָדָ֖יו עַל־יְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to [the] king of Israel, Make ride your hand on the bow; and he made ride his hand, and put Elisha his hands on [the] hands of the king.

en.L: And he said to the king of Israel, "Make your hand ride on the bow." And he made his hand ride [on it], and Elisha put his hands on the hands of the king.
en.B: Then he said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand to the bow." He did so, and Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands.
en.R: Then Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Take hold of the bow." When he had done this, Elisha put his own hands on the king's hands.

decisions.choice: make your hand ride on the bow: take the bow in hand, ready to draw
decisions.reason: The verb means to set something on top of something else, as a rider on a horse. Here it means gripping the bow to shoot.

decisions.choice: Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands: the strength for the shot comes through the prophet
decisions.reason: The prophet's hands over the king's show that the victory the arrow stands for is Yahweh's gift through his word, not the king's own power (verse 17, "the LORD's arrow").

decisions.choice: put your hand to / take hold of; He did so
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture (m1) and do not repeat the whole phrase in the narrative.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פְּתַ֧ח הַחַלּ֛וֹן קֵ֖דְמָה וַיִּפְתָּ֑ח וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֤ע יְרֵה֙ וַיּ֔וֹר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חֵץ־תְּשׁוּעָ֤ה לַֽיהוָה֙ וְחֵ֣ץ תְּשׁוּעָ֣ה בַֽאֲרָ֔ם וְהִכִּיתָ֧ אֶת־אֲרָ֛ם בַּאֲפֵ֖ק עַד־כַּלֵּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Open the window eastward; and he opened. And said Elisha, Shoot; and he shot. And he said, An arrow of victory for Yahweh, and an arrow of victory over Aram; and you will strike Aram in Aphek until finishing.

en.L: And he said, "Open the window eastward." And he opened [it]. And Elisha said, "Shoot." And he shot. And he said, "An arrow of victory for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and an arrow of victory over Aram! And you will strike Aram in Aphek until making an end."
en.B: He said, "Open the window toward the east," and he opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot!" and he shot. Then Elisha said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram! You will strike down Aram at Aphek until you have made an end of it."
en.R: "Open the east window," Elisha said, and the king opened it. "Shoot!" Elisha said, and the king shot. Then Elisha said, "This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s arrow of victory, the arrow that means victory over Aram! You will defeat the Arameans at Aphek until you have wiped them out."

decisions.choice: victory: rescue won by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "deliverer" in verse 5. It is used of the rescue Yahweh gives in battle (1 Samuel 11:13; 19:5). The arrow belongs to Yahweh: the victory will be his.

decisions.choice: eastward ... Aphek: toward Aram
decisions.reason: Aram lay to the north and east of Israel. Aphek was probably the town east of the Sea of Galilee where Ahab had defeated an earlier Ben-hadad (1 Kings 20:26-30).

decisions.choice: you will strike Aram ... until making an end: a promise of complete victory
decisions.reason: The promise is full, but how much of it the king receives depends on what he does next (verses 18-19).

decisions.choice: the LORD's victory; strike down / defeat; Aram / the Arameans
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "for the LORD" into the possessive. Readable names the people, "the Arameans", for the nation "Aram", and says "wiped them out" for "made an end".

decisions.choice: speaker named after the words
decisions.reason: Readable names Elisha and the king in each short exchange so that it is clear who speaks and who acts.

source.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר קַ֥ח הַחִצִּ֖ים וַיִּקָּ֑ח וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לְמֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַךְ־אַ֔רְצָה וַיַּ֥ךְ שָֽׁלֹשׁ־פְּעָמִ֖ים וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Take the arrows; and he took. And he said to [the] king of Israel, Strike [the] ground; and he struck three times and stopped.

en.L: And he said, "Take the arrows." And he took [them]. And he said to the king of Israel, "Strike [the] ground." And he struck three times and stopped.
en.B: "Take the arrows," he said, and the king took them. Then he told the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." He struck it three times and stopped.
en.R: Then Elisha said, "Pick up the arrows." The king picked them up. Elisha told him, "Strike the ground with them." The king struck the ground three times and then stopped.

decisions.choice: strike the ground: beat the ground with the arrows
alternatives: shoot the arrows into the ground
decisions.reason: The king most likely struck the ground with the bundle of arrows. The words could also mean shooting arrows into the ground. Either way the verb is the one used for striking down Aram (verses 17, 19), so each blow stands for a victory.

decisions.choice: stopped: held back
decisions.reason: The king stopped of his own accord after three blows; Elisha had set no number (verse 19).

decisions.choice: with them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the king struck the ground with (m1).

source.text: וַיִּקְצֹ֨ף עָלָ֜יו אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְהַכּ֨וֹת חָמֵ֤שׁ אוֹ־שֵׁשׁ֙ פְּעָמִ֔ים אָ֛ז הִכִּ֥יתָ אֶת־אֲרָ֖ם עַד־כַּלֵּ֑ה וְעַתָּ֕ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים תַּכֶּ֥ה אֶת־אֲרָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And was angry with him [the] man of the God and said, To strike five or six times! Then you would have struck Aram until finishing; and now three times you will strike Aram.

en.L: And the man of God was angry with him and said, "[You ought] to strike five or six times! Then you would have struck Aram until making an end. But now three times you will strike Aram."
en.B: The man of God was angry with him. "You ought to have struck five or six times!" he said. "Then you would have struck Aram down until it was finished. As it is, you will strike Aram down only three times."
en.R: The man of God was angry with him. "You should have hit the ground five or six times!" he said. "Then you would have defeated Aram completely. But now you will defeat Aram only three times."

decisions.choice: to strike five or six times: you should have struck
decisions.reason: The bare verb form states what ought to have been done.

decisions.choice: the king's half-hearted act limits the victory
decisions.reason: The sign was Yahweh's promise put into the king's hands. By stopping at three he showed how little he expected, and he receives what he acted out: three victories (verse 25), not the full end of Aram's power.

decisions.choice: the man of God: the prophet Elisha
decisions.reason: The usual title for Elisha in Kings (4:7; 8:2).

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "only", which the contrast with "five or six times" implies.

decisions.choice: strike ... down
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "strike" for the blows on the ground and "strike down" for Aram, so the link between the sign and the battles stays visible. Readable says "defeat".

source.text: וַיָּ֥מָת אֱלִישָׁ֖ע וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֑הוּ וּגְדוּדֵ֥י מוֹאָ֛ב יָבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ בָּ֥א שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Elisha and they buried him; and bands of Moab would come into [the] land [at the] coming of [the] year.

en.L: And Elisha died, and they buried him. And bands of Moab would come into the land at the coming of the year.
en.B: Elisha died, and they buried him. Now raiding bands from Moab used to come into the land each spring.
en.R: Then Elisha died and was buried. Groups of raiders from Moab used to invade the land every spring.

decisions.choice: bands: raiding parties
decisions.reason: The word means small armed groups that raid for plunder rather than a full army (5:2; 6:23).

decisions.choice: at the coming of the year: in spring
decisions.reason: The year was counted from the spring, and spring was the season when kings went out to war (2 Samuel 11:1; 1 Kings 20:22, 26). The words could also be read as "year after year" or "in that year".

decisions.choice: would come: a repeated event
decisions.reason: The verb describes what used to happen, which sets the scene for verse 21.

decisions.choice: was buried
decisions.reason: Readable uses the passive, as in the death formula, since the Hebrew does not say who buried him.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י הֵ֣ם׀קֹבְרִ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ וְהִנֵּה֙ רָא֣וּ אֶֽת־הַגְּד֔וּד וַיַּשְׁלִ֥יכוּ אֶת־הָאִ֖ישׁ בְּקֶ֣בֶר אֱלִישָׁ֑ע וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ וַיִּגַּ֤ע הָאִישׁ֙ בְּעַצְמ֣וֹת אֱלִישָׁ֔ע וַיְחִ֖י וַיָּ֥קָם עַל־רַגְלָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was, they [were] burying a man, and look, they saw the band, and they threw the man into [the] grave of Elisha; and went and touched the man [the] bones of Elisha, and he lived and stood on his feet.

en.L: And it happened [as] they were burying a man, and look, they saw the band, and they threw the man into the grave of Elisha. And the man went and touched the bones of Elisha, and he lived and stood up on his feet.
en.B: Once, as some people were burying a man, suddenly they saw a raiding band, and they threw the man into Elisha's grave. When the man touched Elisha's bones, he came to life and stood up on his feet.
en.R: One time some people were burying a man, and suddenly they saw a band of raiders. So they threw the body into Elisha's grave. When the dead man touched Elisha's bones, he came back to life and stood up on his feet.

decisions.choice: went and touched: as soon as the body went down and touched
decisions.reason: The two verbs together describe the body coming to rest against Elisha's bones; the second action follows straight on the first.

decisions.choice: the grave: probably a tomb cut in rock
decisions.reason: Tombs were often caves or rooms cut in rock, closed by a stone, where bodies were laid on shelves. Such a tomb could be opened quickly, and the body could touch the bones of one buried earlier.

decisions.choice: he lived: Yahweh's power to give life, shown through his prophet even after his death
decisions.reason: Elisha had raised the Shunammite's son (4:32-37). Even in death the prophet is a sign that Yahweh is still at work for Israel, and that his word to Joash (verses 17-19) will not fail.

decisions.choice: Once / One time; suddenly
decisions.reason: "And it happened" opens a new episode; Balanced and Readable say "Once" or "One time". The word "look" marks a sudden sight and becomes "suddenly".

decisions.choice: the body; the dead man
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the man thrown into the grave was dead.

source.text: וַֽחֲזָאֵל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם לָחַ֖ץ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹאָחָֽז׃

records.literal_gloss: And Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all [the] days of Jehoahaz.

en.L: And Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
en.B: Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel throughout the reign of Jehoahaz.
en.R: Hazael king of Aram treated Israel harshly the whole time Jehoahaz was king.

decisions.choice: oppressed: the story returns to Aram and Israel
decisions.reason: After the Elisha stories the writer takes up again the account of verses 3-7, using the verb of verse 4, and leads into the turn of events in verses 23-25.

decisions.choice: treated harshly
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

source.text: וַיָּחָן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֹתָ֤ם וַֽיְרַחֲמֵם֙ וַיִּ֣פֶן אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם לְמַ֣עַן בְּרִית֔וֹ אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֖ם יִצְחָ֣ק וְיַֽעֲקֹ֑ב וְלֹ֤א אָבָה֙ הַשְׁחִיתָ֔ם וְלֹֽא־הִשְׁלִיכָ֥ם מֵֽעַל־פָּנָ֖יו עַד־עָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And was gracious Yahweh to them and had compassion on them and turned to them for the sake of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and not he was willing to destroy them, and not he cast them from upon his face until now.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was gracious to them and had compassion on them and turned to them, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not willing to destroy them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not cast them from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence until now.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was gracious to them and had compassion on them. He turned toward them for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not yet cast them out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was kind to them and had pity on them. He cared for them because of the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not yet send them away from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

decisions.choice: was gracious ... had compassion ... turned to them: Yahweh's undeserved favor
decisions.reason: Three verbs build up the picture: Yahweh showed favor, felt the tender pity of a parent, and turned his face toward them in care. None of it was earned; the kings of these years did evil (verses 2, 11).

decisions.choice: his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: the promises to Israel's ancestors
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised the land and a people to Abraham and confirmed it to Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 15:18; 26:3-5; 28:13-15). In Egypt he remembered this covenant (Exodus 2:24), and he promised to remember it even after Israel's sin (Leviticus 26:42). This is the only time Kings names the three ancestors together.

decisions.choice: cast them from his presence: send them into exile
decisions.reason: The same words describe the fall of Israel to Assyria and later of Judah to Babylon (17:18, 20, 23; 24:20).

decisions.choice: until now: as yet
alternatives: up to the writer's own day
decisions.reason: The phrase looks ahead: Yahweh held back the exile at this time, though it came later (17:6, 23). It is not a claim that Israel was still in the land when the book was written.

decisions.choice: But; had not yet / did not yet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the contrast with the oppression of verse 22, and turn "until now" into "not yet" (m4).

decisions.choice: kind ... had pity ... cared for them
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the three verbs, and says "the covenant he had made".

source.text: וַיָּ֖מָת חֲזָאֵ֣ל מֶֽלֶךְ־אֲרָ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ בֶּן־הֲדַ֥ד בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Hazael king of Aram, and reigned Ben-hadad his son in his place.

en.L: And Hazael king of Aram died, and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his place.
en.B: When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-hadad became king in his place.
en.R: Hazael king of Aram died, and his son Ben-hadad became king after him.

decisions.choice: Ben-hadad his son: a later king of that name
decisions.reason: Hazael had seized the throne of Aram by killing an earlier Ben-hadad (8:7-15). His son took that name, which earlier kings of Damascus had borne (1 Kings 15:18; 20:1).

source.text: וַיָּ֜שָׁב יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ בֶּן־יְהוֹאָחָ֗ז וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־הֶֽעָרִים֙ מִיַּד֙ בֶּן־הֲדַ֣ד בֶּן־חֲזָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָקַ֗ח מִיַּ֛ד יְהוֹאָחָ֥ז אָבִ֖יו בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הִכָּ֣הוּ יוֹאָ֔שׁ וַיָּ֖שֶׁב אֶת־עָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And returned Jehoash son of Jehoahaz and took the cities from [the] hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael which he had taken from [the] hand of Jehoahaz his father in the war; three times struck him Joash, and he brought back [the] cities of Israel.

en.L: And Jehoash son of Jehoahaz again took the cities from [the] hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, which he had taken from [the] hand of Jehoahaz his father in the war. Three times Joash struck him, and he brought back the cities of Israel.
en.B: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz recaptured from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that Ben-hadad had taken in war from his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash struck him down, and he recovered the cities of Israel.
en.R: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz won back the towns that Ben-hadad son of Hazael had captured in war from his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash defeated Ben-hadad, and he got back the towns of Israel.

decisions.choice: returned and took: took back
decisions.reason: "Returned" with a second verb means doing something again, here taking back what had been lost.

decisions.choice: which he had taken from Jehoahaz: Ben-hadad had captured them in Jehoahaz's reign
decisions.reason: Ben-hadad seems to have led Aram's wars while his father Hazael was still king (verse 3). The cities Hazael took east of the Jordan in Jehu's day (10:32-33) are not said to be won back here; that came later under Jeroboam (14:25).

decisions.choice: three times Joash struck him: Elisha's word fulfilled
decisions.reason: The three victories are exactly what Elisha said after the king struck the ground three times (verse 19).

decisions.choice: Jehoash ... Joash: the same king
decisions.reason: The verse uses both forms of the name (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: struck him down / defeated; recovered / got back
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "strike" so the fulfillment of verse 19 is heard; Readable says "defeated", as there. Readable says "towns", the more usual word for places of this size.
